rationale: A wins because it shows more restraint: it kills the weak take-private story instead of dressing it up as a kept angle, and its strongest line, "Mindbody Says AI Cut Fitness No-Shows by 22%," keeps the actual news in the frame. B has the sharper editor brain in places, especially "Without the baseline, 22% is unpublishable," but it also keeps "Take-private, then automate: what Mindbody is building away from public disclosure," which is mostly inference wearing a trench coat. For a founder deciding what to pitch, A is the cleaner press map; B is the better interrogation memo.
gaps_in_A: "It's Rolling Out to 50,000 Studios" overstates the supplied fact. Mindbody powers booking for 50,000+ studios and salons; the update does not say every one gets or adopts the assistant.
"While Fitness Apps Race to Build AI Coaches" imports an outside trend the update did not supply. It may be true, but this run asked for source-bound angles, not vibes from the AI discourse shelf.

"a tech or business reporter covering AI applications in vertical SaaS" is still a little broad. The angle gets better when it names the sharper sub-beat: vertical SaaS ROI or fitness-operations software.
The ClassPass angle asks the right question, but "AI That Fills Both" is too clever by half and risks implying integration before the proof exists.
gaps_in_B: "Take-private, then automate: what Mindbody is building away from public disclosure" should have been refused, not kept. The set admits "Almost none of this is in hand," which is the editor's cue to kill it.
"studio front desks stopped having time to do" smuggles in a staffing/workload claim the update does not prove. The facts support automated waitlist texts, not a front-desk capacity crisis.
"studios get it whether or not they asked for it" overreads bundled pricing. Bundled into existing tiers is not the same as automatic deployment across all customers.

"now decides which classes fill first" is a strong headline, but it runs ahead of the facts. The update says the assistant texts waitlisted members and suggests class times; prioritization logic is still a proof gap.
